correctness.rationale: Explicit gap potential F is proved to decrease by no more than the cost of any a/b move, with equality at exactly one letter. The forced equality path is the stated word, realizes zero potential after exactly n-G contractions, and no other word has its cost. Cases n=2 and S={0,n-1} and all singleton boundaries are separately covered. Directly executed verify.py checks 130918 nonsingleton subsets for n=2..16 under 4 positive weight pairs; reverse Dijkstra independently verifies all subsets n<=12 under 3 weights; word replays check through n=128. No finite check is taken as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest general primary source Eppstein (1990) gives exact interval BFS for any subset of a cyclically monotone automaton but not a cyclic-gap closed form, positive-weight cost-invariant uniqueness, or an all-subset explicit word. Gusev (2014) concerns pair random-synchronization expectations; Behague–Johnson (2020) discusses k-set rendezvous and Černý worst-case bounds; Ruszil (2021) provides weighted approximation algorithms. The earlier pointwise pair result is a special case, not the new all-subset theorem; the prior exact-image rank reachability statement addresses the reverse image problem, not synchronizing arbitrary given subsets. 2014 Cardoso thesis is a material residual risk because relevant full text remained unavailable.
residual_risks: Cardoso 2014 dissertation discusses exact Černý k-set lower-bound structures, but the complete thesis was not accessible and may contain more explicit pointwise formulas.
An unindexed earlier statement or derivation of some unweighted subset formulas cannot be excluded.

Eppstein 1990 computes unweighted optima for every starting subset algorithmically, so originality depends on explicit all-n symbolic formula and positive-cost-invariant unique optimal word, not the mere ability to compute shortest paths.

value.rationale: Genuinely natural all-subset control-cost problem in an extremal classical automaton. Supplies exact closed-form cost and a uniquely optimal word for every subset and every positive cost ratio, showing a non-obvious simultaneous Pareto optimum on counts of each letter. This is more than a table or straightforward application of a generic shortest-path algorithm: it explains the unique gap-expansion invariant and yields an O(|S|) controller description for all n. Deliberately does not claim other automata or zero-cost cases.
